questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore a different culture and try to live and study in a place that was very different from my home country. I also had to consider that some of my courses were mandatory and needed to be fulfilled during my exchange, and this was one of my options. Additionally, I had heard many positive things about Hong Kong from others.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hong Kong is the perfect place if you want to live in the city but still be close to nature. It's location is great if you want to travel to other countries in Asia as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The orientation organized by the university had limited information and most of the orientation week and further activities were designed to the exchange students living on campus.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a campus tour, introduction to facilities, and orientation about social clubs, when you arrive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The limited amount of orientation during the first weeks makes it very difficult to meet fellow exchange students, especially if you don't stay in the dorms. At the dorms they have their own orientation week, and people get to know each other at this time.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I rented an Airbnb apartment with some fellow KU exchange students off campus. It is quite expensive to live in Hong Kong, so if you want to save money, I suggest staying at the dorms if possible. We wanted to be located more central in the city, and that is why we rented our own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive and small housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The dorms are quite far away from campus (45 min) and even further away from the city center (1 hour). The MTR stops around 1 pm, so if you want to go out it can be a bit difficult to get home, but people managed to do it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before arrival you have applied for the courses you wish to take and then you can change the courses after arrival during the first two weeks. It can be a bit difficult to change the courses afterwards, so choose wisely.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have information online and then you have a coordinator you can contact either in person or by email. They reply quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some classes can get filled up quickly, so be prepared.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level varied a lot between the courses. Some courses were quite easy while others were very different from KU using different programmes you had to learn by yourself.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very creative and innovative, involving and engaging the students a lot. Our own personal thoughts and opinions were a big part  of it compared to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Movies and Psychology
Sexuality, Culture and Diversity
Language and Cognition
Cognitive Psychology
Designing Experiments in Psychology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found the course Sexuality, Culture and Diversity particularly interesting. It covered among others Butler and Foucault, Polygamy, Bisexuality, Transsexuality, Intersex, Pornography, sexual politics and sexual citizenship.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travels to other countries.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is more expensive than I thought. We would eat out everyday because our kitchen didn't work. It is the same price as in DK to eat out and groceries are also more expensive. Transportation is less expensive - especially bus and MTR.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had some interesting events such as monastery visits, Kung Fu lessons, cooking classes and a Kindness Walk where you give back to the homeless.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a variety of different clubs at CityU, but it seemed like most of them were for the locals.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the activities for exchange students which are arranged once in a while, they can be quite fun and is a great place to meat some of the other exchange students - especially if you live off campus. They are also free.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking (Dragon's back, Lion's rock, Jardines lookout, Lantau peak and spend the night in tent on the beach in Sai Kung), visit the islands (Lamma island, Cheung Chau), Big Buddha and Tai O on Lantau island, go to the beach, go out in LKF (Lan Kwai Fong) or Mr. Wong, travel around (Shenzhen, Macao, Beijing), visit the different neighborhoods in Hong Kong. Join some activities outside of uni (e.g. painting course, sports club etc.) - in this way you will meet some more locals.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Even though HK is very international I still found it to be quite the culture shock. But you adjust pretty quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Locals in HK can seem to be quite reserved and keep to themselve but once you talk to them they are super friendly and kind. So you just have to reach out yourself.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People would either sleep during class or talk very loudly and the locals don't take part of oral discussions.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love how HK is a mix of old and new, city and nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Save up money and apply for grants - HK is super expensive and if you would like to travel to other countries it is expensive as well. Consider where you want to live. If you are traveling alone I would suggest living on campus even though it is far away. This is also cheaper.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many of the courses at CityU has continuous assessment meaning a lot of mandatory attendance and many assignments and presentations during the semester, but then they don't really have final exams.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Get to live in a city that is so special. HK is such a special place, I don't know anywhere like it. And also all the people I met - exchange students, locals, teachers, strangers.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making time for everything you would like to do while you are there! Time flies by and there are so many things to explore.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
